name: Ramp
text: Add one high-contrast skip link at the very top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. This fixes keyboard users’ biggest pain point—traversing repeated navigation blocks—without cluttering the interface for sighted users. The trade-off is a small visual footprint, but it’s invisible to most and critical for a few, so it’s worth it.

name: Reader
text: One high-contrast skip link fails users who rely on screen readers when the target isn’t programmatically labeled—it lands them in a silent void. A better fix is a visible skip link *plus* a named landmark (`<main role="main">`) so screen readers announce the jump; settle it by testing with VoiceOver/NVDA and confirming both keyboard and AT users reach the content.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps to a named `<main role="main">` landmark. This solves keyboard users’ navigation trap while giving screen reader users a clear destination—no silent voids. The trade-off is a tiny extra DOM node, but it’s invisible to everyone except assistive tech, where it matters most.

name: Reader
text: A high-contrast skip link to `<main role="main">` still risks forcing keyboard users to tab through *all* interactive elements before reaching the skip link—especially if the navigation is long or dynamic. A better fix is a *first-tab* skip link that appears only after the first tab press, paired with a visible skip link for sighted keyboard users. Settle it by testing with both VoiceOver and keyboard-only users to confirm it doesn’t create a new trap.
